E1.evidence: Issue #102 (corot, 2013-10-04): "battery info is on /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0, and not on default /proc/acpi/battery/BAT0" and "charging symbol doesn't appear in the dashboard". rk4an gives the reproducing environment (clean Ubuntu 12.04.3, kernel 3.8.0-31-generic) and the missing files; maintainer corot confirms and lists the processing defects (comment 27193014) and fixes them in 928306b.

E2.interface_kind: wire protocol field (kernel ACPI battery attribute files under /proc/acpi/battery and /sys/class/power_supply)
E2.evidence: linux_hardware/scripts/laptop_battery.py (ROS node, turtlebot repo) reads battery data from files provided by the Linux kernel's ACPI battery driver. The provider-side file names, value scale and status string format cross the boundary. The minimal resolving change is not only a device-path rebinding: besides moving the default path from /proc/acpi/battery/BAT0 to /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0 (param default and launch args), the consumer's code had to follow different attribute names (0c0f532: `charge_full`, `charge_full_design`, `current_now`, `charge_now` fallbacks), rescale values (928306b: `/10e5`) and strip the status string (`.lower().rstrip()`). Not deployment_wiring, not build, not firmware.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: rk4an (issue #102 comment 26799473): "We just made a clean install of **Ubuntu 12.04.3 LTS** and the default kernel are **3.8.0-31-generic** instead of previous **3.2.0-53-generic-pae** (default netbook ASUS 1025C)"; the consumer's default path targets the older layout (fix comment in minimal.launch: "/proc/acpi/battery/BAT0 in 2.6 or earlier kernels").

E4.evidence: Observed: "charging symbol doesn't appear in the dashboard" (issue body); rk4an: "But  the new **laptop_hardware.py** file doesn't work because some files was renamed"; corot: "Current doesn't get possitive when charging, so the charging symbol never appears" and "_Design Capacity_ is lower than _Capacity_; I suppose this is wrong".

loudness_evidence: The source reports missing and wrong battery information ("charging symbol doesn't appear in the dashboard"; "Current doesn't get possitive when charging, so the charging symbol never appears"; "_Design Capacity_ is lower than _Capacity_") without any diagnostic from tooling. (The consumer's code at 2.2.2 would logwarn and shut down if the /proc path is missing, but no such message is shown in the source.)

resolution.summary: Consumer-side, two commits: 0c0f532 (merge of PR #104) falls back to charge_full / charge_full_design / current_now / charge_now when the energy_* / power_now files are absent; 928306b divides all sysfs values by 10e5, strips the trailing end-of-line from status, reads design capacity from *_full_design and last-full capacity from *_full, and changes the default path to /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0 (~acpi_path default in laptop_battery.py and the battery arg in minimal.launch / minimal_with_appmanager.launch). Kernel unchanged.
resolution.evidence: Merged by the maintainer (corot, commit message "Issue #102: Battery info fixed for new laptops"); tfoote on PR #104: "+1 partial fix for #102". rk4an on PR #104: "Not tested on other version of Ubuntu sorry." No comment shows the resolved revision working with an identified kernel.

notes: consumer_built_against is documented as the previous kernel the reporter ran ("3.2.0-53-generic-pae"); ABI 3.2.0-53 has three package tags in the Ubuntu precise kernel repository (Ubuntu-3.2.0-53.79/.80/.81), so a descriptive label is used. The resolved label is the kernel named in PR #104's title ("fix renamed files for battery info on Ubuntu 12.04.3 LTS - Kernel 3.8"). Primary-source caveat: in mainline drivers/acpi/battery.c (v3.2 and v3.8 alike) the sysfs properties are charge_* / current_now when `battery->power_unit == ACPI_BATTERY_POWER_UNIT_MA` and energy_* / power_now otherwise, and /proc/acpi/battery exists only with CONFIG_ACPI_PROCFS_POWER ("Deprecated power /proc/acpi directories"); so the charge_* naming the reporter calls a rename depends on the battery hardware, while the move away from /proc follows the kernel build. The classification follows the reporter's observation on the upgraded system. corot's statement "Values must be divided by 10e6" is not tied to a stated kernel; the fix divides by 10e5 (=10^6). corot also reports the effect "Current doesn't get possitive when charging, so the charging symbol never appears", which follows from the status string with trailing EOL mapping to 0 (DISCHARGING in LaptopChargeStatus.msg) and the rate being negated. Other composition in the source, not a condition of this case: laptop_battery -> dashboard via topic laptop_charge (LaptopChargeStatus), where the missing charging symbol and the design-capacity < capacity display are observed; these are downstream effects of the values read from the kernel. Earlier related fix: https://github.com/turtlebot/turtlebot/pull/61 (commit "Making laptop battery script work with the new /sys filesystem organization.", present in the consumer's history as bdf3080), which added the /sys reader that assumed energy_* / power_now files. Inventory elements use the `api:` form for kernel attribute files (no canonical form for OS files exists in the schema).
